title: Subgraph with private state doesn't have a proper state at the last node
observed_behavior: A level-2 graph is compiled with a private pydantic state (CodeFeedbackAgentPrivateState) and the parent node's return writes that private key. When the level-2 graph is used as a node of a level-1 graph whose state is OverallState, the merge rejects the update because it does not write any parent key: InvalidUpdateError: Must write to at least one of the OverallState keys.
structure_focus: Compiled subgraph whose state schema is a private schema with no overlapping keys or output mapping to the parent; nested subgraph boundaries
notes: Closed; maintainer answer: the last node's update is applied to the level-1 state, but a graph used as a node must still respect its parent's state. Fix with input/output transformations (or schemas that share keys). The OP's code snippet is not directly runnable (n(...) wrappers in the shown graph), and the body describes three levels; the fixture keeps the essential two-level boundary: an OverallState parent containing a compiled child whose state is a private schema that shares no keys with the parent. Classified user_graph because the fix is state-boundary design, not a framework defect.
